RUN.about: Cut by the lifecycle of one HTTP request — a caller configures ky, makes a request, then consumes the response — with retry logic and error handling branching from the request step.

AUTHORED.title: Setting Up Ky
AUTHORED.sub: Import ky, create instances with custom defaults, merge and normalize options
AUTHORED.detail: The default export is a singleton `KyInstance` built by `createInstance()`. Each call or method shortcut deep-merges caller options with instance defaults, then `Ky.create()` runs init hooks, normalizes everything, and constructs the `Request`.

issues.title: AbortSignal.any fallback drops earlier signals
issues.detail: When `AbortSignal.any` is unavailable and multiple signals are combined via `.extend()`, only the last signal is used (`signals.at(-1)`). Earlier signals are silently dropped, so aborting them does nothing.

rows.detail: `AbortSignal.any([userSignal, controllerSignal])` creates a managed signal for both user aborts and timeouts.

rows.title: Set deadline
rows.detail: `totalTimeout` starts now: `performance.now() + totalTimeout` is the deadline for the entire pipeline.

children.detail: Ky creates an internal `AbortController` and merges its signal with the user's via `AbortSignal.any()`, then attaches this managed signal to every Request so both user aborts and timeout aborts cancel the fetch.

rows.value: After a timeout, the old controller is spent; a new one is created and a fresh managed signal wired before the next attempt

rows.label: Feature-gated
rows.value: Requires AbortSignal.any; without it no controller is created and timeout cannot abort in-flight requests

children.title: Lifecycle Hooks
children.sub: Five hook types intercept the request at different stages of the pipeline
children.detail: Hooks run as arrays in order — `init` is synchronous while the other four are async and raced against `totalTimeout`. A hook can replace the request, short-circuit with a response, force a retry, or transform an error.

code.label: #runBeforeRequestHooks: may return Response or replace Request
#runAfterResponseHooks: clones response for each hook, may force retry
#throwProcessedError: runs beforeError hooks in sequence
All five hook type signatures

anatomy.caption: The five hook types and what they can do
rows: Request | Response | stop | options update | void
Before any error is thrown to caller

anatomy.caption: Hook execution order for a request that fails once then succeeds

rows.label: beforeRetry hooks (retryCount: 1)
rows.note: can return stop, Request, Response, or options update

rows.label: beforeRequest short-circuit
rows.value: Returning a Response skips fetch entirely; remaining beforeRequest hooks are also skipped

rows.label: afterResponse force retry
rows.value: Returning ky.retry() throws ForceRetryError internally, bypassing method and status checks on retry eligibility

rows.label: beforeRetry can stop
rows.value: Returning ky.stop resolves the promise with undefined; body shortcuts then throw a helpful TypeError

rows.label: Hook response not retried
rows.value: A Response from a hook with a non-ok status throws HTTPError immediately without entering the retry loop

rows.label: All async hooks raced
rows.value: Every async hook is raced against totalTimeout via #raceWithTotalTimeout; a slow hook can time out the request

children.title: Executing The Fetch
children.sub: The #fetch method clones for retry, wraps with upload progress, and calls fetch with timeout
children.detail: Each attempt runs through `#fetch()`, which clones the request for a possible retry via `ReadableStream.tee()`, wraps the body with upload progress, races against the effective timeout, and converts raw network errors to `NetworkError`.

code.label: #fetch: clone, wrap, timeout race, error conversion
#retry: calls #fetch and catches errors for retry flow
#wrapRequestWithUploadProgress: pipes body through progress stream
#retryFromError: delay, reset controller, beforeRetry hooks, then #retry again

rows.title: Cancel previous body
rows.detail: Releases the unused upload body from a prior attempt via cancelBody().

rows.title: Clone for retry
rows.detail: request.clone() via ReadableStream.tee() when retryLimit > 0. Skipped when retries disabled to avoid buffering large uploads.

rows.title: Wrap upload progress
rows.detail: If onUploadProgress is set and request streams supported, pipes body through a TransformStream counting bytes.

rows.title: Calculate effective timeout
rows.detail: Math.min(timeout, remainingTotalTimeout). Returns undefined when both are infinite, skipping the timer entirely.

rows.title: Race fetch against timeout
rows.detail: Calls timeout() which starts a setTimeout and races it against fetch(request). If the timer wins, AbortController fires.

rows.title: Validate response
rows.detail: Checks the result is a Response — a custom fetch returning something else gets a clear TypeError.

rows.title: Wrap network errors
rows.detail: A raw TypeError from a dropped connection is wrapped as NetworkError for consistent recognition and beforeError hooks.

anatomy.caption: Error types produced by #fetch
rows: TypeError: must resolve with a Response

issues.title: Stream body buffered when retries enabled
issues.detail: When the body is a ReadableStream and retries > 0, request.clone() calls ReadableStream.tee() which buffers the entire stream in memory. For large uploads this causes high memory usage. Setting retry: 0 skips the clone.

children.title: Timeout And Abort
children.sub: Per-request timeout and totalTimeout budget constrain every async step in the pipeline
children.detail: The `timeout` option (default 10 000 ms) limits each fetch attempt via `setTimeout` + `Promise.race`. The `totalTimeout` option limits the entire pipeline including hooks, retries, and body reads, measured from construction.

code.label: timeout(): races fetch against setTimeout, aborts on loss
#raceWithTotalTimeout: races any async operation against the remaining budget
#getEffectiveTimeout: min of per-request timeout and remaining total
#getRemainingTotalTimeout: Math.max(0, deadline - now)
delay(): async sleep with abort signal support, used between retries

anatomy.caption: How the two timeout mechanisms cooperate

rows.label: timeout default
rows.value: 10 000 ms. Can be false to disable. Maximum is 2 147 483 647 (max 32-bit int).

rows.label: totalTimeout default
rows.value: false (off). When set, starts at construction and counts hooks, retries, delays, and body reads.

rows.label: Hooks also bounded
rows.value: Every async hook (beforeRequest, afterResponse, beforeRetry, shouldRetry) is raced against totalTimeout.

rows.label: Body reads bounded
rows.value: #raceBodyRead applies the effective timeout to .json(), .text(), etc. A slow download can time out.

rows.label: Retry delay checked
rows.value: If the retry delay alone would exhaust the remaining budget, Ky waits that long then throws TimeoutError without starting another fetch.

rows.label: Late response cancelled
rows.value: timeout() discards a response arriving after the timer won, calling cancelBody() to prevent a leak.

children.title: Body And Progress
children.sub: Upload and download progress tracking, response size limits, and body lifecycle management
children.detail: Upload and download progress wrap body streams through `TransformStream` pipes counting bytes, while `maxResponseSize` is enforced by a separate transform that throws `ResponseSizeError`. Unused bodies are cancelled via fire-and-forget `body.cancel()` to prevent memory leaks.

code.label: withProgress: TransformStream counting bytes for progress callbacks
streamRequest: wraps upload body with duplex half streaming
streamResponse: wraps download body, adjusts for content-encoding
limitResponseSize: enforces maxResponseSize via TransformStream
cancelBody: fire-and-forget release of unused body streams
getBodySize: calculates byte size for FormData, Blob, string, etc.

rows.title: Wrap upload body
rows.detail: If onUploadProgress is set and request streams supported, pipes request.body through withProgress which counts each chunk.

rows.title: Enforce response size limit
rows.detail: If maxResponseSize is set, response body piped through a TransformStream that throws ResponseSizeError when the total exceeds the limit.

rows.title: Track download progress
rows.detail: If onDownloadProgress is set, response body piped through withProgress. Content-encoded responses report totalBytes as 0.

rows.title: Preserve response metadata
rows.detail: copyResponseMetadata patches .url, .redirected, .type, and body methods on the new Response wrapping the transformed stream.

rows.title: Cancel unused bodies
rows.detail: cancelBody() releases streams from previous attempts, replaced responses, and timed-out operations. Locked-stream failures are silently swallowed.

rows: Approximation: boundary + headers + part sizes (off by ~14 bytes/part in Bun)

rows.label: Progress callback shape
rows.value: {percent, totalBytes, transferredBytes} — percent is 0..1, capped at 1-epsilon until the final flush event

rows.label: Content-encoded downloads
rows.value: When content-encoding is not identity, totalBytes is 0 since content-length counts compressed bytes on the wire

rows.label: Null body statuses
rows.value: 101, 103, 204, 205, 304 — response body is never wrapped, no progress or size enforcement

rows.label: Upload requires duplex
rows.value: Upload progress needs request stream support (duplex: half). Skipped for keepalive, no-cors, and non-Request inputs.

AUTHORED.sub: Read the response body via .json(), .text(), .bytes() shortcuts, validate with Standard Schema, and track download progress

Each shortcut sets an `Accept` header, awaits the response, reads the body with timeout/abort racing, and optionally validates JSON via Standard Schema.

children.detail: Each shortcut is attached in `Ky.create` by looping over `getSupportedResponseTypes()`. Non-json types call `response[type]()` via `#raceBodyRead`; the json shortcut reads as text first, then parses and optionally validates.

rows.title: Set Accept header
rows.detail: Sets Accept to the MIME type for this shortcut (e.g. `application/json`), but only if the request has already been dispatched (clone exists).

rows.title: Await the response
rows.detail: `await result` resolves the ResponsePromise to the Response from `#run()`. Throws TypeError if `ky.stop` left it undefined.

rows.title: Read with race guard
rows.detail: Non-json types call `response[type]()` via `#raceBodyRead`, which races the native body method against `timeout` and `totalTimeout`, wrapping network drops as `NetworkError`.

rows.title: Parse JSON (json only)
rows.detail: Reads body as text, then calls `parseJson` option or `JSON.parse`. Empty text with a schema and no custom parser yields `undefined` instead of a parse error.

rows.title: Validate schema (json only)
rows.detail: If a Standard Schema was passed, calls `schema['~standard'].validate()` and throws `SchemaValidationError` on failure.

children.title: Download Progress
children.sub: Track response body download via onDownloadProgress stream wrapping

rows.title: Check Retry Limit
rows.detail: If `retryCount >= min(retry.limit, retryLimit)`, re-throw the error. No retry.

rows.detail: A `ForceRetryError` from `afterResponse` skips all remaining checks and returns its custom delay or the default backoff.

rows.detail: If the request method is not in `retry.methods`, re-throw. POST and PATCH are excluded by default.

rows.title: shouldRetry Callback
rows.detail: If configured, called with `{error, retryCount}`. Exact `false` throws, exact `true` overrides later checks, anything else uses defaults.

rows.detail: `TimeoutError` is retried only when `retryOnTimeout` is `true` or `shouldRetry` returned `true`.

rows.detail: `HTTPError` checks status against `statusCodes`. For statuses in `afterStatusCodes`, server timing headers are parsed. 413 without a timing header is not retried.

rows.detail: `NetworkError` is retried with the default delay. Any other unrecognised error type is re-thrown to prevent retrying programming bugs.

children.title: Exponential Backoff
children.sub: Default delay formula with optional jitter and an upper bound
children.detail: The default formula is `0.3 × 2^(attempt-1) × 1000` ms, producing 300ms, 600ms, 1200ms per attempt. Full jitter randomizes between 0 and the computed value, custom jitter falls back on invalid results, and `backoffLimit` caps the final delay.

children.title: Retry Loop
children.sub: The mechanics of #retryFromError: wait, reset state, run hooks, and re-fetch
children.detail: After the delay is computed, `#retryFromError` checks the `totalTimeout` budget, waits the delay (abortable by user signal), resets the abort controller if needed, applies forced-retry custom requests, runs `beforeRetry` hooks, then calls `#retry` → `#fetch`.

code.label: #retryFromError: full retry execution flow
beforeRetry hook loop with return-value dispatch

rows.title: Check Total Timeout
rows.detail: If `totalTimeout` budget is zero, throw `TimeoutError` immediately without starting another attempt.

rows.title: Budget Guard
rows.detail: If `retryDelay >= remainingTimeout`, wait the remaining time and throw `TimeoutError` — avoids a wasted fetch.

rows.title: Wait
rows.detail: Sleep for the computed delay. Only the user's abort signal can interrupt; the internal timeout signal is not used for the wait.

rows.title: Reset Abort Controller
rows.detail: If the previous attempt timed out (abort controller is aborted), create a fresh one and update the request's signal.

rows.title: Apply Custom Request
rows.detail: For `ForceRetryError` with a custom `Request`, replace the current request. Headers are not sanitized — the caller opted in.

rows.title: Run beforeRetry Hooks
rows.detail: Each hook receives `{request, options, error, retryCount}` and can return a value that changes the retry (see table below).

rows.title: Re-fetch
rows.detail: Increment `retryCount`, call `#retry()` → `#fetch()`, which clones the request for the next possible retry.
